description: Pore geometry of one rigid framework from the structure library with Zeo++ (one Voronoi decomposition, built-in radii). You choose the structure, probe radius, sampling and time limit. Returns largest included/free sphere diameters (Angstrom), percolating channels and dimensionality, accessible/non-accessible surface area (m2/g), probe-occupiable pore volume (cm3/g), pore size distribution, pocket-blocking sphere count, caution flags, evidence and cost. Cheap (seconds to minutes on one CPU), so use it to screen structures before GCMC or DFT. Geometry only: it does not predict adsorption, and every number depends on the probe radius you choose.

structure_id.description: Structure from the library; Zeo++ needs a CIF entry.

probe_radius_angstrom.description: Probe radius for channel accessibility, surface area and pore volume. The repository N2 recipes use 1.86.

psd_probe_radius_angstrom.description: Probe radius for the pore size distribution.

sampling.description: Monte Carlo sample counts: fast for screening, standard matches the validated recipes, fine for final numbers.

high_accuracy.description: Zeo++ -ha; recommended for frameworks with mixed atom sizes.

block_pockets.description: Also compute RASPA blocking spheres for inaccessible pockets (needed before GCMC).

grid_crosscheck_spacing_angstrom.description: Independent distance-grid check of surface area and volume at this spacing, or null to skip. Slower for large cells.

timeout_seconds.description: Wall-time limit for the Zeo++ job; it is reserved from the compute budget.
